L’histoire de K-Reau, marque provençale: The story of K-Reau, a Provençal brand born in Mallemort: places in Marseille, on the Côte Bleue and across Provence as line drawings on ceramic decorative tiles, with their names in calligraphy.
One place. One memory. One K-Reau.
Une marque provençale de carreaux décora: A Provençal brand of illustrated decorative tiles, born between the Durance, the Luberon and the Alpilles.
Dessin au trait de l’île des Embiez, ave: Line drawing of the island of Les Embiez, with its name in calligraphy
Some places stay with you. The harbour of your summer holidays, the cove you know by heart, the hill you can see from your window, the town where it all began.
K-Reau est né d’une envie simple : donne: K-Reau started from a simple wish: to give the places that stay with us a spot in our homes. Not a postcard tucked away in a drawer, not a mass-produced shop souvenir, but a clean drawing that keeps the essence of a landscape, one you enjoy looking at every day.
K-Reau est imaginé à Mallemort, dans les: K-Reau is designed in Mallemort, in the Bouches-du-Rhône, where the Durance river separates the Luberon from the Alpilles. Here, the light draws everything: the shade of plane trees on a village square, limestone ridges at sunset, the sparkle of the sea as you reach the Côte Bleue.
En Provence, le carreau fait partie de l: In Provence, tiles are part of the home. The red terracotta tomettes of old farmhouses, the cement tiles of traditional kitchens, the earthenware handed down through families: ceramics here have always told the story of places and the people who live in them. Our ceramic decorative tiles pick up that thread in our own way: a black line, a white background, and a name.
Le trait, la céramique, la calligraphie: The line, the ceramic, the calligraphy
Tout commence par le choix d’un lieu, to: It all begins with choosing a place, always a real place, one we love and recognise at first glance. We draw it as a single line, stripping away everything that is not essential until only its outline remains: the Bonne Mère on her hill, the ridge of the Sainte-Victoire, the arches of the Vallon des Auffes.
Le dessin est ensuite accompagné du nom: The drawing is then paired with the name of the place, written in calligraphy, and UV-printed on a 15 × 15 cm glossy white ceramic tile. Each tile is carefully packed and sent in a kraft gift box, ready to give. It can stand on a shelf or sideboard, or hang on the wall.
